questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore Japan and Japanese culture with an anchor-point, which would be to live somewhere in Japan in a prolonged period of time

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, people were very friendly and helpful - a lot of information was written in Japanese, which was not ideal for me, as I couldn't understand it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance from my host-university in the weeks leading up to the start of study semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, I found housing through online rental portals - everything went smoothly with that.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's great, you have more freedom with regards to potential curfews and what insurances you want to pay for.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It seems like a standard registration process, you apply for the courses you want, which fit within your schedule, and then follows a period of accepting/rejecting the possible courses with regards to the limits of participation within each course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My host university had a whole department working on helping the exhange students navigate the online course registration portals. So it was quite easy to seek out help, when you inevitably got confused.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I think I only missed out on 1 or 2 classes out of the 7 I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you can, I would recommend applying for the language courses, they are really good - definitely my favourite classes of the ones I had.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was alright, nothing spectacular.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar, though the classes were smaller than I'm used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
16906:Cross-cultural Studies (GA)(Cross-cultural Studies: Physical, Mental and Theoretical approaches for intercultural understanding with the elements of the Martial arts and the Arts.)
10229:Lecture for Humanities (LD) § 10230:Selected Problems in Humanities (LD) (Literary trends in Japanese modern novel (from late Meiji to early Showa period))
13288:IR18-GE203 Japanese Culture (RA) § 13289:IR-FS203 Japanese Culture (RA)
10672:Lecture for Humanities (LJ) § 10673:Selected Problems in Humanities (LJ)
10237:Lecture for Humanities (LH) § 10238:Selected Problems in Humanities (LH) (Manga Expressions: Exploring Manga History)
10015:Lecture for Humanities (LA) § 10016:Selected Problems in Humanities (LA)
17124:Japanese I-1(Comprehensive) (KZ)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all, especially the language courses - they really helped me feel more at home and navigate the rest of my time is Japan better. The only course I would not recommend is the course 10229:Lecture for Humanities (LD) § 10230:Selected Problems in Humanities (LD) (Literary trends in Japanese modern novel (from late Meiji to early Showa period)), as the professor was very unprofessional and out-right vicious, it was not a pleasant experience to have this course because of this.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The scope of obligatory insurance costs surprised me a bit in Japan, seeing as I'm already insured from back home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was really cheap, most things were really cheap actually.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I played football and did fitness - both were fairly simple to get into if you knew the right people around campus - there were always a pretty heavy language barrier between exchange and native students, which could be hard to navigate.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the gym facilities, they are very clean and you always feel safe there. They are also located at campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the shrines, go to the mountains, grab a drink at the crazy chicken Izakaya. Have a lot fun - visit other large cities in Japan, I really recommend Hiroshima and Takayama!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, although it guess it depends on how well you can adjust to very different cultural practices.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, and try to learn as much Japanese as you can!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure I found the differences challenging. I really enjoyed how a lot of things were not like I'm used to back home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think the food culture was a bog deal for me, I really loved it!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to find accommodations away from campus dorms, take some Japanese language courses while in Kyoto and don't take the academic courses too serious - you have more than enough time to travel around the parts of Japan you want while you're there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find a local Onsen that you like early on within your stay, it is the best way to relax and de-stress.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure I can answer that question in this format - but maybe the friends we made along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Navigating Japanese official documents sent by mail.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
